title: Checkpoint: Testing and Debugging
intro: Check that you can write useful tests, pick good test cases, use pytest, and debug with print, tracebacks, and logging.

questions.question: What happens when this code runs?
questions.explanation: The parentheses make a non-empty tuple, which is always true, so the assert never fails. Write assert price == 20000, "wrong price".

questions.question: Which assertion passes for 0.1 + 0.2?
questions.explanation: 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004, so == 0.3 fails. pytest.approx (or math.isclose) compares with a tolerance.

questions.question: This prints False. What is the best way to test the average?
questions.explanation: Floats have tiny rounding errors, so compare them with math.isclose() (or pytest.approx in pytest).

questions.question: A registration form must reject negative ages. Which is correct?
options: assert age >= 0 in the form handler
raise ValueError when age is below 0
wrap assert age >= 0 in try/except: pass
questions.explanation: assert statements are removed when Python runs with -O, so real validation needs if and raise.

questions.question: A function gives a discount for orders of 100000 som or more. Which set of test values is best?
questions.explanation: Bugs hide at boundaries. Testing just below, at, and just above the limit catches mistakes like > instead of >=.

questions.question: Which test is better for tax(price) = price * 12 // 100?
questions.explanation: An expected value copied from the code repeats its bugs. Use a plain number you worked out by hand.

questions.question: You run pytest in a folder with totals.py containing def check_total(). pytest says "collected 0 items". Why?
options: pytest is not installed in this project
Test files and functions must be named test_*
The assert inside the function is wrong
Tests must be inside a TestCase class
questions.explanation: pytest only collects files and functions whose names start with test. "no tests ran" is not success.

questions.question: pytest runs this test. What is the result?
options: It passes, but the assert is never checked
It fails because balance is not 999
pytest reports an error in the test
questions.explanation: withdraw() raises inside the with block, so the next line never runs. Put checks after the with block.

questions.question: What appears on the screen when this script runs?
questions.code:
import logging
logging.info("order created")
logging.warning("stock low")
questions.explanation: Without basicConfig the level is WARNING, so info() messages are dropped.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: The = inside an f-string field prints the expression text followed by its value, which is handy for print debugging.
